description.narrative: The partnership will advance gender equality and the empowerment of women and girls, contributing directly to SDG Target 5.4, whichcalls for recognizing and valuing unpaid care and domestic work through public services, infrastructure, and social protection policies, and promoting shared responsibility within households and families as nationally appropriate. Lao PDR has emerged as a leader in driving transformative change in the care economy, earning international recognition for its pivotal role in championing the ‘ASEAN Declaration on Strengthening Care Economy and Resilience Towards ASEAN Community Post-2025’ during its tenure as ASEAN Chair. At the national level, Lao PDR conducted a National Household Care Survey in 2024, which provided critical insights into the distribution and societal impacts of unpaid care and domestic work. Building on these efforts, the 2024 national consultation on the care economy, convened by the Lao Women’s Union (LWU), ESCAP, and Oxfam in Laos, produced a robust set of policy recommendations identifying entry points for transformative change. Additionally, Lao PDR has taken proactive steps to localize the ASEAN Declaration on Care byorganizing a National Dissemination Workshop on ASEAN Declaration and outlining steps towards the adoption of a National Action Plan on Strengthening the Care Economy. The objective of this agreement is to empower policymakers within national and local governments to advance gender equality by driving the adoption of enabling policies that value unpaid care and domestic work and promote investments in the care economy. Specifically, this partnership aims to support the drafting and validation of a National Action Plan on Strengthening the Care Economy through workshops with key stakeholders, including government agencies, civil society organizations, women’s rights groups, and the private sector. Furthermore, it seeks to share learnings with other countries and stakeholders through participation in regional and international conferences and learning events. This project will contribute to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals in Lao PDR and the broader Asia-Pacific region by: Strengthening multi-stakeholder engagement to develop and validate a cohesive National Action Plan on Care; Increasing the knowledge and capacity of decision-makers by equipping them with tools, evidence, and frameworks to effectively implement the plan and advocate for policy reforms and Promoting cross-sectoral collaboration among national and local governments to ensure an integrated, multi-stakeholder approach to addressing unpaid care work and advancing the care economy.

participating-org.narrative: ESCAP-UN Economic and Social for Asia and the Pacific

Oxfam has had a presence in Lao PDR for longer than most INGOs, with both Oxfam in Belgium (OBE) and Oxfam Australia (OAU) beginning programming and establishing offices in the late 1980s. Oxfam’s vision is of a Laos in which all citizens – particularlywomen, the marginalised and discriminated groups – are able to claim their right to access opportunities and resources so as to overcome all forms of poverty and injustice.
Since 2015, the work of Oxfam in the country is governed by the Oxfam Country Strategy (2015-2019).We seek transformative changes in policies, practices and beliefs in ways that fundamentally improve the lives of poor and marginalised women and men, and ensure that all citizens have the same opportunities to enjoy their rights. Todo so, Oxfam focuses its work on four Domains of Change: Citizen Participation and Civil Society Development, Gender Justice, Resilient Communities and Sustainable Development, and Responsible Investment.
For this project, Oxfam in Laos will support theexpansion of the influencing work and public campaign on advocating for more inclusive social protection and access to social protection of the most marginalized workers. National public events will be organised, such Eliminate Violence Against Women Day(EVAW), and digital platforms will be used to socialize the information, and stir discussion and dialogue among rights holders, government stakeholders and policy makers. The campaigns will be implemented nationwide and in the provinces where Oxfam in Laos works. Target groups include marginalized workers, youth,women, CSOs as well as government stakeholders.
